title: Ada and the Postcard
premise: Emrys Almeida, a marine biologist who fled a public scandal fifteen years ago, lives by small safe steps: turtle counts, tide charts, and a quiet lease on the cottage above Ada Okonkwo's failing seaside bakery. When a postcard postmarked eleven years earlier finally surfaces—misdelivered, water-stained, written in Emrys's own hand to a person they never told the truth to—it forces open the past they buried, including the wrongful blame that cost them their career. As the bakery lease runs out and a developer circles, Emrys and Ada dig into who intercepted the letter and why, finding justice not in courts but in testimony, restitution, and community. In the end, Emrys testifies at last, the bakery is saved as a co-op, and they stop lending pieces of their heart and give the whole thing—to Ada, and to the town that becomes their found family.
about_author: Ines Underhill is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who now writes romance from a rented room above a chandlery on the Cornish coast. Their fiction is known for salt-weathered settings, slow-burning tenderness, and characters who learn that safety is a place you build with other people.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A dawn turtle survey establishes Emrys's careful, measured life: routines, checklists, distance from people. They pay rent late to Ada, who teases them gently. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline; the reader sees how much Emrys has shrunk their world to stay safe.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Bakes at Four
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada fights to keep her bakery open against rising rent and a developer's interest, feeding fishermen and strays alike. She notices Emrys watching her shop from the seawall but never coming closer. Emotional beat: Ada's stubborn warmth and her own guarded heart beneath the flour-dusted cheer.

chapters.title: Water-Stained
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Renovating the cottage after a storm, Emrys finds a postcard wedged behind the skirting board—postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to them, never delivered. The handwriting is their own. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past knocking politely, then insistently, at the door.

chapters.title: What I Never Sent
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, flashback woven through present. The postcard was meant for Dr. Marguerite Voss, the mentor Emrys loved and lost when a falsified data scandal destroyed both careers—and Emrys took the fall silently. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing; the first crack in Emrys's armor of small safe steps.

chapters.title: Bread and Bad News
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada finds Emrys shaken on her doorstep at closing time and, without asking questions, feeds them. The developer's offer letter arrives pinned to her door. Emotional beat: unexpected intimacy; two guarded people recognizing each other's damage.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ninety days notice: the landlord has sold to Halloran Development. Ada rallies her regulars while privately panicking about losing the shop her late mother built. Emrys offers to help with paperwork. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; the stakes of the town itself.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Address
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Following the postcard's thread, Emrys learns Marguerite died three years ago—but her sister, Nell Voss, kept all of Marguerite's papers, including letters suggesting the scandal was engineered. Emotional beat: hope arriving too late and exactly on time; justice becoming possible outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Pieces Lent
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada and Emrys grow close over bakery ledgers and archive boxes, but Emrys flinches from every step toward commitment, offering help but never themselves. Ada names it plainly: 'You lend pieces.' Emotional beat: tender confrontation; Ada refusing crumbs of a person she wants whole.

chapters.title: Nell Voss Keeps Everything
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At Nell's house upriver, Emrys confronts eleven years of unsent replies from Marguerite—she believed in Emrys's innocence until the end. Among her papers: evidence pointing to colleague Dr. Peter Rask, now celebrated, whose signature is on the doctored dataset. Emotional beat: vindication and rage braided together.

chapters.title: Halloran's Man
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The developer's local agent turns out to be connected to Rask—Halloran's money laundered through the same network that ruined Emrys. The bakery fight and the old scandal are one fight. Emotional beat: the personal becoming structural; anger finding a target.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Rask, tipped off, arrives in town charming everyone, including the council reviewing the bakery lease. He offers Emrys quiet rehabilitation in exchange for silence. Emotional beat: temptation of the easy exit; Emrys almost takes the deal that would betray everything again.

chapters.title: The Tide Chart Confession
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada tells Emrys about her mother's eviction, the debt she inherited, why she can't lose the bakery—and asks Emrys to stop hiding behind turtles. Emrys tells her the whole truth of the scandal for the first time. Emotional beat: mutual unmasking; the beginning of trust rather than transaction.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys tries to return to routine—the survey, the checklist—and finds the rituals hollow now. A hatchling release at night, witnessed with Ada, breaks something open: some things only survive by rushing toward the sea. Emotional beat: turning point; choosing risk over ritual.

chapters.title: Testimony, Unsworn
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At the packed council meeting on the lease, instead of the planned legal argument, townspeople testify—one by one—about what the bakery means. Emrys stands and begins telling the truth about Rask publicly. Emotional beat: justice as chorus; the community becoming the court.

chapters.title: Rask Fights Dirty
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Rask retaliates: an anonymous complaint suspends Emrys's research permit, and Halloran accelerates demolition permits. Ada's oven fails; the shop limps along on a single working burner. Emotional beat: the squeeze tightening; despair tested against stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Archive Box
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Nell delivers Marguerite's final notebook, which documents Rask's falsification directly and names a second witness still alive: the retired lab technician, Mrs. Okafor, living two towns over. Emotional beat: the past handing them a weapon; courage requiring witnesses, not just evidence.

chapters.title: Mrs. Okafor Decides
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They visit Mrs. Okafor, who was paid off and shamed into silence years ago. Ada, not Emrys, convinces her—not with arguments but with bread, patience, and the story of her mother. Okafor agrees to speak. Emotional beat: found family forming around shared injury; healing as recruitment.

chapters.title: Everything or Nothing
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. On the eve of the hearing, Rask makes a final offer: full reinstatement, funding, reputation—if Emrys withdraws. Emrys realizes staying invisible was never really an option, and that they've been offered their old life back at the price of the new one. Emotional beat: the whole-heart choice made explicit; refusal.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Climax. Before the council and a journalist Okafor contacted, Emrys presents Marguerite's notebook and Okafor's testimony; Rask unravels under cross-examination by the crowd's questions. The council votes to reject the demolition permit pending investigation. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice arriving loud, communal, and earned.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Rising Dough
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Rask is suspended pending inquiry; Halloran withdraws. The town proposes buying the building as a community co-op—with Emrys quietly putting their settlement savings in first. Ada finds out. Emotional beat: abundance after scarcity; generosity revealed rather than performed.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys stops lending pieces: they ask Ada properly, on the seawall where they first watched each other, offering not help or protection but partnership—co-signing the co-op, sharing the cottage, sharing the life. Emotional beat: vulnerability completed; love as a decision repeated daily.

chapters.title: Postmarked Today
chapters.summary: Both POVs, alternating. One year later: the co-op bakery opens under a new sign, Emrys's permit restored and research expanded with Okafor's granddaughter as an intern, Nell at the head table. Ada mails a postcard to no address at all—'to whoever needs it delayed'—tucked behind the skirting board for the next finder. Emotional beat: full-circle resolution; inheritance passed forward, family chosen, hearts spent whole.
